items.prompt: When is the sky dark so we can see the stars?

figure.alt: The Moon and stars in a dark sky.

options.why: At midday the Sun is high and the sky is bright.
At lunchtime it is daytime and the sky is bright.
After breakfast it is daytime.

hints: Think about when you go to bed.
Stars are hard to see when the sky is bright.
Ask: when does the sky turn dark?
items.explanation: At night our side of the Earth faces away from the Sun. The sky is dark, so we can see the stars.

items.prompt: Does it happen in the day or at night? Sort the cards.

items.text: the Sun is in the sky

hints: Think about what you see and do in the day.
Then think about what happens when it is dark.
Start with the stars. When can you see them?
items.explanation: In the day the Sun is in the bright blue sky and children go to school. At night the stars come out, owls hunt and most people sleep.

items.prompt: Why do we have day and night?

options.text: The Sun goes around the Earth each day.
options.why: Many people once thought this. The Earth spins, and the Sun only seems to move.

options.text: The Sun switches off at night.
options.why: The Sun always shines. Our side of the Earth turns away from it.

options.text: Clouds cover the Sun at night.
options.why: Night comes even when there are no clouds.

hints: The Sun always shines.
Think about a ball turning in front of a torch.
Ask: which one moves, the Earth or the Sun?
items.explanation: The Earth spins round. When our side faces the Sun, we have day. When it turns away from the Sun, we have night.

items.prompt: How many hours does the Earth take to spin round once?
hints: One spin gives us one day and one night.
Think about how many hours there are in one whole day.
A day has 12 hours on the clock twice.
items.explanation: The Earth spins round once in about 24 hours. That gives us one day and one night.

items.prompt: How does the Sun seem to move across the sky?

options.text: It rises in the west and sets in the east.
options.why: The Sun rises in the east.

options.text: It stays in one place all day.
options.why: The Sun seems to move across the sky during the day.
The Sun rises in the east.

options.text: It rises in the east and sets in the west.

hints: Think about where the Sun is in the morning.
Sunrise and sunset happen on opposite sides of the sky.
Remember: the Sun rises in the east.
items.explanation: The Sun seems to rise in the east, cross the sky and set in the west. It only seems to move because the Earth is spinning.

items.prompt: Put the times of day in order, starting with sunrise.
hints: The day starts when the Sun comes up.
Midday is in the middle of the day.
Put sunrise first. What comes after it?
items.explanation: The day goes sunrise, morning, midday, afternoon and sunset. Then it is night.

items.prompt: At midday the Sun is high in the sky. What are shadows like?

options.why: Long shadows happen when the Sun is low, in the morning and evening.
At sunset the Sun is low, so shadows are long.
Evening shadows are long because the Sun is low.

hints: Shadows change as the Sun moves across the sky.
Shine a torch from high above a toy. Is the shadow long or short?
Ask: is the Sun high or low at midday?
items.explanation: At midday the Sun is high, so shadows are short. In the morning and evening the Sun is low, so shadows are long.

items.prompt: When is each animal most active? Sort the cards.
hints: Some animals sleep in the day and wake at night.
Think about which animals you see on the way to school.
Start with the bat. When do you see bats flying?
items.explanation: Butterflies, bees and hens are busy in the day. Owls, bats and fireflies are active at night. Night animals are called nocturnal.

items.prompt: An animal active at night and asleep in the day is ___.
hints: Owls and bats are like this.
The word is used in science for night animals.
It starts with noc and has 9 letters.
items.explanation: An animal that is active at night is nocturnal. Owls, bats and fireflies are nocturnal.

items.prompt: It is daytime in Jakarta. What is it like on the other side of the Earth?

figure.alt: The Sun shining on one side of the Earth.

options.why: The other side is turned away from the Sun.
Day and night do not decide the seasons.
The other side faces away from the Sun.

hints: Only one half of the Earth faces the Sun at a time.
Jakarta is on the half that faces the Sun now.
Ask: what is it like on the half facing away?
items.explanation: Only the half of the Earth that faces the Sun has day. The other side faces away, so it is night there.

items.prompt: The Earth also travels around the Sun. How long does one trip take?

options.why: One day is one spin of the Earth.
One hour is much too short. The trip is very long.
One week is 7 spins of the Earth.

hints: One spin takes one day. The trip around the Sun is much longer.
Think about how often your birthday comes.
Ask: what do we call 365 days?
items.explanation: The Earth takes about one year, or 365 days, to travel around the Sun. It spins round once every day on the way.

items.prompt: Why can we not see the stars in the daytime?

options.text: Stars go away in the day.
options.why: The stars are still there. The sunlight hides them.
Stars shine all the time.
Even on a clear day we cannot see stars.

options.text: The Sun's light is too bright.

hints: Stars shine all the time.
Think about seeing a torch beam on a sunny day.
Ask: what makes the daytime sky so bright?
items.explanation: Stars shine all the time. In the day, the Sun's light is so bright that we cannot see the faint stars.

items.prompt: In Jakarta the Sun rises at about 6 o'clock in the morning. It sets at about 6 o'clock in the evening. About how many hours of daylight are there?

figure.alt: Sunrise at 6 o'clock in the morning and sunset at 6 o'clock in the evening.

hints: Count the hours from morning to evening.
From 6 o'clock to 12 o'clock is 6 hours.
Now count from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock in the evening.
items.explanation: From 6 in the morning to 12 is 6 hours, and from 12 to 6 in the evening is 6 more. 6 and 6 make 12 hours of daylight.

items.prompt: Rafi sees the Sun low in the east. What time of day is it?

options.why: At midday the Sun is high in the sky.
In the evening the Sun is low in the west.
At midnight the Sun cannot be seen.

hints: The Sun rises in the east.
Low in the sky means near the start or end of the day.
Ask: which part of the day starts with sunrise?
items.explanation: The Sun rises in the east. Seeing it low in the east means it has just risen, so it is morning.

items.prompt: Which one is true about the Sun and the Earth?

options.text: The Sun moves around the Earth every day.
options.why: It looks that way, but the Earth is spinning.

options.text: The Earth spins, so the Sun seems to move across our sky.
The Sun goes under the sea at night.
options.why: The Sun is far away in space. Our side of the Earth turns away from it.

options.text: The Sun is closer to the Earth at night.
options.why: At night our side of the Earth faces away from the Sun.

hints: What we see is not always what is really happening.
Think about a car ride. The trees seem to move past you.
Ask: which one is really moving each day, the Earth or the Sun?
items.explanation: The Earth spins once a day. As it spins, the Sun seems to move across our sky, just like trees seem to move past a moving car.

items.prompt: Draw the Sun and the Earth. Colour the side of the Earth that has night.

criteria.label: Draws the Sun and the Earth
Shows the side facing the Sun as day
Colours the side facing away from the Sun as night

hints: The side of the Earth facing the Sun gets light.
The other side is in darkness.
items.explanation: The half of the Earth that faces the Sun has day. The half that faces away has night. As the Earth spins, places move from day to night.

items.prompt: The ___ gives us light and heat in the daytime.
hints: We see it in the sky when it is day.
It is very bright and hot.
You should never look straight at it.
items.explanation: The Sun gives us light and heat. At night we cannot see it because our side of the Earth faces away.

items.prompt: Tap 2 things you can see in the night sky.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: sun, moon, star and rainbow.

hints: Think about what you see when it is dark.
One is round and bright and one is a tiny light.
It is not the Sun or a cloud in the day.
items.explanation: We see the Moon and the stars at night. The Sun is out in the day.

items.prompt: Label the pictures with day or night.
hints: The Sun is out in the daytime.
The Moon is out at night.
Look at each picture.
items.explanation: We see the Sun in the day and the Moon at night.

items.prompt: What do we call the time when the Sun comes up?

options.why: Sunset is when the Sun goes down.
Midnight is in the middle of the night.
Moonrise is when the Moon comes up.

hints: It happens in the morning.
The Sun rises.
It is the start of the day.
items.explanation: Sunrise is when the Sun first appears in the morning sky.

items.prompt: What do we call the time when the Sun goes down?

options.why: Sunrise is when the Sun comes up.
Midday is when the Sun is high.
Dawn is the start of the day.

hints: It happens in the evening.
The Sun sets.
It gets dark soon after.
items.explanation: Sunset is when the Sun goes down in the evening.

items.prompt: In which direction does the Sun seem to rise?

options.why: The Sun seems to set in the west.
The Sun does not rise in the north.
The Sun does not rise in the south.

hints: Rising is the opposite of setting.
It sets in the west.
Look at a compass.
items.explanation: The Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.

items.prompt: Which of these helps us see at night?

options.why: Rainbows need sunlight.
The sky is dark at night.
A shadow is not a light.

hints: We need a light source.
Rainbows are in the day.
Lamps shine.
items.explanation: A street lamp makes light, so it helps us see in the dark.

items.prompt: Why do shadows move during the day?

options.text: The Sun seems to move across the sky.

options.why: Objects stay the same size.
Wind does not move shadows.
The Sun makes the shadows.

hints: What makes the shadow?
The Sun appears to move.
The Earth spins.
items.explanation: As the Earth spins, the Sun seems to move across the sky. This makes shadows move.

items.prompt: Nina sees the Moon in the sky in the afternoon. Is that possible?

options.text: No, the Moon is only out at night.
options.why: It is sometimes out in the day.

options.text: No, it must be a cloud.
options.why: It can be the Moon.
It can happen at any time of year.

options.text: Yes, the Moon can be in the sky in the day.

hints: The Moon goes round the Earth.
It is not always at night.
Look for pale shapes.
items.explanation: The Moon is in the sky for part of the day and part of the night. We can often see it when the Sun is up.

items.prompt: Which animal is active at night?

options.why: A hen is awake in the day.
A squirrel is awake in the day.
A butterfly flies in the day.

hints: It has big eyes.
It hoots.
Hens sleep at night.
items.explanation: Owls hunt at night and sleep in the day. They are nocturnal.

items.prompt: When is the animal awake? Sort the cards.
hints: Bats fly in the dark.
Butterflies need the Sun.
Hens go to roost at night.
items.explanation: Owls, bats and hedgehogs are awake at night. Butterflies, squirrels and hens are awake in the day.

items.prompt: Choose all the things we can see in the night sky.
hints: Rainbows need sunlight.
The Sun has set.
Stars twinkle.
items.explanation: We can see the Moon, stars and aeroplane lights at night. Rainbows and the Sun are seen in the day.

items.prompt: Put the Sun's day in order.
hints: Sunrise comes first.
Midday is when the Sun is high.
Midnight is last.
items.explanation: The Sun rises in the morning, is highest at midday and sets in the evening. Then it is midnight.

items.prompt: Match the time to what the Sun is doing.
pairs: the Sun is on the other side
hints: Midday means the middle of the day.
Sunset is when it goes down.
At midnight it is dark.
items.explanation: At sunrise the Sun comes up and at midday it is highest. At sunset it goes down. At midnight it is on the other side of the Earth.

items.prompt: The Earth ___ once every 24 hours. This gives us day and ___.
hints: The Earth turns.
Day is followed by something dark.
Read slowly.
items.explanation: The Earth spins once every 24 hours. This gives us day and night.

items.prompt: Where is the Sun in the sky?
head: Time
The Sun is
hints: It rises low.
At midday it is overhead.
At midnight we cannot see it.
items.explanation: The Sun is low at sunrise and sunset and high at midday. At midnight it is on the other side of the Earth.

items.prompt: Jo measures a stick's shadow at 9 am, 12 noon and 3 pm. At 9 am the shadow is long. At noon it is short. At 3 pm it is long again.

options.text: The Sun seems to move across the sky.

hints: Read the middle sentence.
The Sun is high at noon.
The stick stays the same.
items.explanation: At noon the Sun is high, so the shadow is short. The Sun seems to move, so the shadow changes.

items.prompt: How many hours are there in half a day?
hints: One day is 24 hours.
Half means share by 2.
Think 12 + 12.
items.explanation: A day has 24 hours. Half of 24 is 12 hours.

items.prompt: Tap the planet we live on.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: Sun, Moon, Earth and another planet.

hints: It is not a star.
It has water and land.
It is blue and green.
items.explanation: We live on planet Earth.

items.prompt: The Earth spins. This makes day and ___.
hints: Day is followed by something dark.
It is the opposite of day.
It starts with n.
items.explanation: As the Earth spins, one side faces the Sun and has day. The other side has night.

items.prompt: It is midday in Jakarta. Rina looks at her shadow. How does it look?

options.why: The Sun is high, so the shadow is short.
The Sun makes a shadow.

options.text: it is twice as tall as she is
options.why: The Sun is high, so the shadow is short.

hints: Where is the Sun at midday?
High means short.
Think of a lamp overhead.
items.explanation: At midday the Sun is high in the sky, so shadows are short.

items.prompt: Bayu faces the rising Sun. He turns around. Which way is he facing now?

options.why: East is where the Sun rises.
He turned half way round.
He turned half way round.

hints: The Sun rises in the east.
Turning around is the opposite.
The opposite of east is west.
items.explanation: The Sun rises in the east. When Bayu turns around he faces west.

items.prompt: The Earth spins once in 24 hours. How many times does it spin in 3 days?
hints: One day is one spin.
Count the days.
3 days.
items.explanation: Each day is one spin, so 3 days is 3 spins.
